text.p: Hundreds of residents in the Bangladesh capital Dhaka drove away more than 300 prostitutes from a well known brothel area on Monday, police and witnesses said.
Witnesses said hundreds of residents gathered from around the red-light "Kandupatti" area at Golokpal lane in old Dhaka city and drove the prostitutes from their cluster of homes.
"There was no violence. The prostitutes did not resist and came out of their homes with (their) belongings," said a newspaper photographer.
He said several police watched the eviction from a distance and did not intervene.
Police said the residents living near the brothel complained that the prostitutes' presence and behaviour threatened their social life and the moral values of their children.
"It's true the brothel has been the breeding ground for all sorts of unsocial activities and crimes," one officer said.
But Hasina Begum said: "This is an act of cruelty. Where do we live now. I have been living in this brothel for the past 17 years."
